rationale: Iteration 0 has no race telemetry, so this is a conservative baseline built from the contract. Sensors: five 12 mm sensors (smaller than the 25 mm tape, so the readings stay informative) spaced 0.02 m apart across x = -0.04 to +0.04, placed 0.05 m ahead of the axle so steering reacts before the wheels reach the bend. Weights follow x/0.02, so the signal is negative when the tape is on the right and positive when it is on the left, matching the steering convention. Gains: kp = 2.5 gives a moderate steering response, ki = 0 avoids integral windup on bends, and kd = 0.2 damps oscillation. base_speed = 1.3 (about 65% of the PWM ceiling) aims for the roughly 1.5 m/s average the 3 s limit needs while leaving headroom for turns. line_loss = last_direction so the robot keeps searching toward the side it last saw the tape. Geometry: 0.12 m track, 0.03 m wheels, 0.12 m body width (wider body allows more off-track margin), 0.18 m body length, 0.8 kg mass. Expected result: completes the oval and s-bend with few line losses; slalom and speed may expose too much or too little gain. Next measurements: completion_time and max_error will show whether speed or steering is the binding limit, and steering_oscillation will show whether kp or kd needs changing.
